The authors investigated the sampling convergence by extending the sampling range from 2.0×10^3 to 2.3×10^4 snapshots and refining the resolution from 50 to 105 Hz.
The authors identified four global convergence states with increasing sampling range: Initialization, Transition, Stabilization, and Divergence.
The Stabilization state is the optimal state for modal convergence, where the DMD output becomes independent of the sampling range.
The authors found that over-sampling causes algorithmic instability, as the temporal dimension (n) approaches and transcends the spatial dimension (m), leading to divergent and meaningless output.
The authors suggest a resolution of 15 frames per cycle for target activities in most engineering implementations.
The authors conducted the parametric study using the turbulent free-shear flow over a prism as the test case, which is a canonical nonlinear system in fluid mechanics.
The authors employed Large-Eddy Simulation with Near-Wall Resolution (LES-NWR) to obtain high-fidelity data for the parametric study on the DMD algorithm.

The comprehensive parametric study took over 16 months to complete, utilizing over 800,000 core-hours on two 64- and 80-core high performance computers, excluding the time dedicated to the LES-NWR simulation.
The authors conducted rigorous tests on the numerical results to certify the fidelity of the DMD input data, ensuring that the parametric study was driven by accurate data.

The authors provide a comprehensive and reliable reference for future applications of the DMD algorithm, especially in the engineering domain, by addressing the critical gaps in the understanding of sampling range, resolution, and convergence.

The prism wake is a simplistic yet sophisticated test case, as it includes various fluid phenomena like stagnation, separation, reattachment, and vortex roll-up, while also being common in engineering applications.
The authors assessed the convergence of the DMD modes using both global and mode-specific behaviors, including the l2-norm of the reconstruction error and the I-criterion for dominant mode selection.
The authors found that the convergence of the sampling range and resolution are mutually independent.
The authors chose a moderately high Reynolds number (Re=22,000) for the test case, as it accommodates high-fidelity simulation with common computing power for engineering applications.
The authors selected a spanwise dimension of 4D for the computational domain, which is sufficient for the particular flow during the shear layer transition.
